review: Independent rereview of privacy token-provider resolution
resolution_evidence: AppleAdsReporter.start reserves activeLease and enqueues acquireToken on the utility global queue while holding only the short lease/state critical section. It no longer directly calls the token provider on its caller.

acquireToken checks transport generation immediately before token invocation, releases the consent lock before the synchronous provider call, and reacquires the lease gate after it returns. setEnabled(false) does not acquire a provider-owned lock or wait for token completion.

Post-provider withLease rejects a revoked generation, and activeLease equality prevents an obsolete provider result from modifying a newer active run. HTTP task creation/resume remains inside the consent gate.

Repeated start calls within the current generation are coalesced by activeLease reservation before dispatch. Off/on creates a new generation, so a new run may proceed while the previous uncancellable provider finishes locally.

The two held-provider tests exercise start/revocation returning before provider release and a new generation completing while an old provider result is discarded. All 14 authored native test methods were inspected; none were run.
Other six privacy-scope product/configuration files retain the hashes from the initial independent review.
consent_boundary: The generation is checked immediately before entering the uncancellable platform provider. Revocation can happen after that authorization or while the call is running; the already-authorized local call may finish, but its result cannot create old-generation HTTP, retries, events or sent-marker writes. The implementation does not promise atomic prevention of every underlying platform instruction racing that boundary.
